newsitem.title: UK: UK GILTS THIS WEEK- FOCUS ON BOE INFLATION REPORT.
newsitem.headline: UK GILTS THIS WEEK- FOCUS ON BOE INFLATION REPORT.

text.p: UK gilts will be at the mercy of the Bank of England this week, with any significant upward progress contingent on the central bank repeating hints made last week that rates are on hold for now.
Analysts said the Bank's quarterly inflation report and press briefing by chief economist Mervyn King on Wednesday will be the key focus for markets, despite the rash of economic data due beforehand.

"Although it's a reasonably busy week on the data side, the main focus will be the Bank of England inflation report and the minutes from the July meeting of the MPC (monetary policy committee)," said Merrill Lynch gilts analyst Steven Andrew.

The Bank of England raised interest rates by a further quarter point to 7.0 percent last Thursday and hinted heavily that the level of rates was now consistent with the government's inflation target of 2.5 percent.
But other UK data due out this week, including retail prices on Tuesday and average earnings and unemployment figures on Wednesday, could promote volatility in the meantime.
September gilt futures were steady at the start of the week, in contrast to last week's turbulent sessions, and stood unchanged in Monday afternoon trade at 114-09/32.
After pushing up and outperforming on Thursday, gilts fell nearly a full point to finish 28/32 lower on Friday.
Economists said the market was still fraught with danger, especially the short end.
A Reuter poll of 26 London-based economists conducted on Friday found 17 expect further rate rises.
And while some estimated the peak in the current cycle as high as 8.5 percent, others said they worried that the Bank could grow complacent.
Gilts, and the short end in particular, looked set to head lower if Wednesday's inflation report failed to confirm the favourable interest rate outlook.
"I do feel they will still highlight the risks on upside and they might also use some fairly robust language in doing so," said Jonathan Loynes, economist at HSBC Markets.
"There could therefore be scope for disappointment in the market as it could be a little more hawkish than the market is expecting."

Economists said they expected the gilt/Bund spread to remain fairly stable this week, hovering around the middle of recent range and not heading much lower due to continuing concerns over the interest rate outlook and inflation.
The spread widened by one basis point on Monday to 152 basis points.
"I don't see any particular movement in the spread -- I don't think we can maintain it at the low 140s, where we initially rallied to last week," Andrew said.
"Largely this is because of the uncertainty over the rate outlook and because the numbers out on Tuesday for inflation we don't expect to be particularly friendly looking."

UK producer price numbers released on Monday morning had little impact on the gilts market. The data showed slightly higher than expected output prices figures, with input prices falling in line with expectations due to the strength of sterling last month.

"Overall, these numbers (PPI) suggest there is little threat to the overall inflation outlook from producer level. The main worry, as ever, will be tomorrow's RPI data," said David Coleman, CIBC chief economist.

On the international front, analysts said the market would also be watching economic data due out from the United States, including Wednesday's retail sales and producer prices, for indications that the U.S. economy was maintaining favourable growth and inflation trends.

"I think we'll be keeping one eye on those (U.S. figures) as well as our own data to see if there's any move away from the strong growth, low inflation scenario expected in the U.S., but the international data overall is going to be fairly benign," Loynes said.
